name: assigns by preferred indexer and returns top k
test:
processed, busiest, top_k, percentage = document_indexing_queue(3, [1, 2, 3, 7], [5, 4, 3, 2], 2)
assert processed == 4
assert busiest == 0
assert top_k == [0, 1]
assert abs(percentage - 75.0) < 1e-9

name: drops documents when all indexers are busy
input: two indexers, later arrivals before either release
test:
processed, busiest, top_k, percentage = document_indexing_queue(2, [0, 0, 1, 4], [5, 5, 1, 1], 2)
assert processed == 2
assert busiest == 0
assert top_k == [0, 1]
assert abs(percentage - 100.0) < 1e-9

name: release boundary uses finish time less than or equal to arrival
input: an indexer finishing exactly at the next arrival
test:
processed, busiest, top_k, percentage = document_indexing_queue(3, [0, 1, 2, 3], [3, 3, 3, 1], 1)
assert processed == 4
assert busiest == 0
assert top_k == [0]
assert abs(percentage - 50.0) < 1e-9

name: wraps around to lower-numbered available indexers
input: preferred index and higher indexers busy while indexer zero is free
test:
processed, busiest, top_k, percentage = document_indexing_queue(4, [0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 3], [2, 10, 10, 10, 1, 1], 4)
assert processed == 5
assert busiest == 0
assert top_k == [0, 1, 2, 3]
assert abs(percentage - 100.0) < 1e-9
